narrative.overview:
Every file in Tandem is handled like an archived object that carries its own chain of custody. The dashboard reads as an accession register rather than a SaaS file list. It sits on a cool acid-free grey board, with white paper panels drawn in 1px rules and ink-dark text. Condensed catalogue caps are used for accession numbers, version tags and column heads. Identity is the system's main subject. Each save is marked by who held the file, an assistant or a person, and that mark keeps the same shape and colour wherever it appears.

The surface is dense, quiet and daylight-legible: 14px body on a 20px line, tabular numerals everywhere, flat panels and almost no decoration. Colour is scarce and always means something. Slate gives structure and selection, verdigris marks agents, ink-blue marks humans, ochre marks unsaved or contested work, and accession red appears only on things you can press. The one authored motion is the custody record sliding into place when you select a file.

The build rejects the neutral SaaS file table with pill badges: actor identity is a fixed mark plus a catalogue label, never a coloured lozenge.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey board, white paper panels, 1px rules, 4px corners.
Two custody identities: verdigris squares for agents, ink-blue circles for humans; hollow squares for unrecorded versions.
Archivo Narrow caps for codes, versions and column heads; Public Sans for everything else.
Accession red reserved for pressable primary actions.
Flat at rest; shadow only on floating layers.
One motion: the custody record's 180ms slide-in.

rules.name: The Red Means Press Rule
rules.body: Accession red appears only on things you can press: the primary button and the link. It never marks status, identity, headings or decoration, and a disabled button loses it.

rules.name: The Two Holders Rule
rules.body: Verdigris belongs to agents and ink-blue to humans, everywhere and for nothing else. The shape (square or circle) always carries the identity alongside the hue, so it reads without colour vision.

rules.name: The Catalogue Caps Rule
rules.body: Archivo Narrow caps label data: codes, versions, actor class and column heads. It is never set as an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, and never used for running text.

rules.name: The Paper On Board Rule
rules.body: Panels, the register and the custody record never cast shadows. They are set apart by white against grey and a 1px rule. Shadows are only for things that float: dialogs, toasts and menus.

dos: **Do** put Accession Red only on pressable primary actions, and strip it from disabled ones.
**Do** show every actor through the identity plate: mark, AGENT/HUMAN catalogue label, name, and "for {person}" for agents.
**Do** keep custody marks at fixed sizes: 8px for every version, 12px for the head.
**Do** draw a chain of custody as one 2px vertical rule with marks centred on it, newest first.
**Do** set codes, versions, column heads and actor class in Archivo Narrow 600 caps at 12px with 0.06em tracking.
**Do** separate surfaces with white paper on the grey board and a 1px rule, at 4px corners.
**Do** mark diffs with a −/+ gutter marker as well as the ochre or slate band.
**Do** use ochre for unsaved and contested work, never red.
donts: **Don't** render actor identity as coloured pill badges or lozenges; the build replaced them with marks and catalogue labels.
**Don't** use verdigris or ink-blue for anything except agent and human identity.
**Don't** convey custody by colour alone; the square-versus-circle shape is required.
**Don't** say "online" or show live presence dots; the plate is attribution, and times read "last edited" or "saved".
**Don't** use catalogue caps as an eyebrow or kicker above headings.
**Don't** add shadows to panels, the register or the custody record; shadows belong to dialogs, toasts and menus.
**Don't** add motion beyond the custody-in slide and functional spinners, and honour reduced-motion.
